title: 140 km/h Winds Expected as Arnab Nears India #Shorts
description:
Where will Cyclone Arnab land today?

Cyclone Arnab is forecast to cross India's north Andhra Pradesh coast today, with winds expected to reach up to 140 km/h (about 87 mph). Andhra Pradesh has closed schools and says 1,763 cyclone shelters are ready, while Odisha has a red alert in six districts. Forecasts can change, so follow IMD bulletins and local authorities.

Footage: stock clips and file imagery for illustration (Pixabay, NASA), not of the actual event.

Sources: PTI via ThePrint; Open Magazine; ANI via LatestLY; India.com live blog; India Meteorological Department (IMD), mausam.imd.gov.in

Hopeverse Media is made with AI: the hosts, voices and some visuals are AI-generated, and every script is fact-checked before it goes up. Made by AI. Made with hope.

script:
SCHEDULE: 08:05 IST Wed 28 Oct 2026 (Short 5 of 6 today).

PRE-PUBLISH CHECK (REQUIRED): Before going live, check the latest IMD bulletin at mausam.imd.gov.in. If Arnab has already crossed, weakened below severe, or the landfall area has changed, HOLD the post and flag it to Mr. Hope. Do not publish forecast wording after the event has happened.

SCRIPT (Arjun and Meera only, about 48 s):
ARJUN: "Cyclone Arnab is forecast to hit India's coast today, with winds expected to reach up to 140 kilometres an hour."
MEERA: "Where exactly, and how strong?"
ARJUN: "India's weather office, the IMD, expects Arnab to cross the north Andhra Pradesh coast today, Wednesday, 28 October."
ARJUN: "On Monday it was a severe cyclonic storm, and the IMD expected it to strengthen into a very severe one before landfall. 140 km/h is about 87 miles per hour."
MEERA: "Who is on alert?"
ARJUN: "Andhra Pradesh has shut schools, and its disaster authority says 1,763 cyclone shelters are ready. Next door, Odisha has a red alert in six districts, with heavy rain forecast."
MEERA: "What should people on the coast do?"
ARJUN: "Follow IMD bulletins and local authorities, stay off the sea, and follow evacuation orders immediately. Forecasts can change."
ARJUN: "Late October is peak cyclone season in the Bay of Bengal."
MEERA: "Follow Hopeverse for the world's news, explained daily."

CAST: Arjun (calm, unhurried explainer; muted solid shirt, neutral news desk; face from reference photo) and Meera (warm but subdued questions; muted outfit, same desk). No Lumen, no Navigator. Hosts max ~30% of runtime.

EDIT PLAN (Mr. Cut): 9:16, 21 shots, cut every 2-3 s. Always-on corner tag "Based on IMD forecasts reported 26-27 Oct. Check mausam.imd.gov.in". Hook: NASA Worldview satellite cyclone + "LANDFALL EXPECTED TODAY", then Arjun; big-text "up to 140 km/h (forecast)", "140 km/h ≈ 87 mph", "1,763 shelters ready", "Odisha: red alert, 6 districts"; OpenStreetMap maps labelled "FORECAST" (north Andhra Pradesh, then Odisha); all generic rain/sea/coast/school clips labelled "FILE FOOTAGE", satellite clips not of Arnab labelled "FILE IMAGERY"; three advice cards (Follow IMD bulletins / Stay off the sea / Follow evacuation orders); URL card; two-shot + logo outro. Muted blue-grey grade, low ambient pulse at -18 to -20 dB under voice, bold white captions. No damage, flooding or victim footage; use text-card backups if a clip shows any. Credit NASA Worldview, OpenStreetMap contributors and stock sites on screen.

THUMBNAIL: Number-led, no face. Calm satellite cyclone swirl on the left, simple map of India's east coast with a small marker near north Andhra Pradesh, small "FORECAST" label; large "140 km/h" in amber on deep navy, white swirl. No damage, victims or alarm graphics.

PINNED COMMENT: "Forecasts can change. Follow the IMD (mausam.imd.gov.in) and local authorities for the latest. Which do you check first when a storm is coming: A) official weather bulletins or B) local alerts?"
